name: Militaria, Weapons & Military Vehicles
description: Questions covering: Main battle tanks, Assault rifles, Fighter aircraft, Attack helicopters...

questions.question: What is the family name of the main battle tank series that includes the M1?
questions.explanation_correct: The M1 series of American main battle tanks is known as the Abrams family. This name identifies the tank line rather than a specific variant.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are also tank family names, but they refer to different national designs. They are not the M1 tank family name.

questions.question: Which designer surname is associated with the AK series of assault rifles?
questions.explanation_correct: The AK series is associated with Mikhail Kalashnikov. His surname became the standard designation for the rifle family.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other surnames belong to notable Soviet firearms designers, but not the AK series. They are linked to different weapons.

questions.question: What is the nickname of the Grumman F-14 fighter aircraft?
questions.explanation_correct: The Grumman F-14 is commonly known as the Tomcat. This nickname is widely used in aviation and military history.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices are nicknames of different fighter aircraft. They do not refer to the F-14.

questions.question: What model nickname is commonly associated with the AH-64 attack helicopter?
questions.explanation_correct: The AH-64 attack helicopter is commonly called the Apache. That nickname identifies the type in military service.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are helicopter names, but they belong to different models or roles. They are not the AH-64's nickname.

questions.question: Which common designation is used for the Israeli submachine gun developed by Uziel Gal?
questions.explanation_correct: The Israeli submachine gun designed by Uziel Gal is called the Uzi. Its common designation became the weapon's widely recognized name.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are also submachine guns, but they are different designs. They are not the common designation of the Israeli weapon.

questions.question: Which ship class name is associated with Japan's largest battleship design of World War II?
questions.explanation_correct: The Yamato class was the Japanese battleship class that included the famous lead ship Yamato. It is one of the best-known battleship classes in naval history.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are battleship classes from different navies. They do not name the Japanese class in question.

questions.question: What is the name of the U.S. air-defense system designated MIM-104?
questions.explanation_correct: Patriot is the U.S. air-defense system associated with the MIM-104 designation.
questions.explanation_incorrect: S-300, Thunderbird and Rapier are different surface-to-air missile systems.

questions.question: Which inventor surname is tied to the hand-cranked multiple-barrel gun from the 19th century?
questions.explanation_correct: The hand-cranked multiple-barrel gun is named after Richard Gatling. His surname became attached to the weapon's design.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other surnames are also famous in firearm history, but they are linked to different guns. They are not the inventor of the Gatling gun.

questions.question: What nickname is commonly used for the Boeing B-52 strategic bomber?
questions.explanation_correct: The Boeing B-52 is commonly nicknamed the Stratofortress. The nickname is the aircraft's well-known service name.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are bomber nicknames as well, but they refer to different aircraft. They are not the B-52's nickname.

questions.question: What is the name of the U.S. anti-tank guided missile designated FGM-148?
questions.explanation_correct: The FGM-148 Javelin is a portable anti-tank guided missile system.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Stinger is an air-defense missile; Dragon and TOW are different anti-tank systems.

questions.question: Which U.S. aircraft carrier class includes USS Nimitz (CVN-68) and USS George H.W. Bush (CVN-77)?
questions.explanation_correct: Both ships belong to the nuclear-powered Nimitz class.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The Kitty Hawk, Enterprise and Gerald R. Ford names refer to other carrier classes or ships; Enterprise and Ford are also nuclear powered.

questions.question: What is the common name for the M109A6 self-propelled howitzer?
questions.explanation_correct: The M109A6 is a 155 mm self-propelled howitzer known as Paladin.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Crusader was a later U.S. artillery program; Bishop and Sexton were different WWII-era vehicles.

questions.question: Which weapon family is the best-known shoulder-fired surface-to-air missile system produced by Raytheon?
questions.explanation_correct: Stinger is a portable surface-to-air missile system designed for individual use. It is one of the most recognized shoulder-fired missile families.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are missile or air-defense systems, but they are not the requested family. They fit the same category without being the correct one.

questions.question: Which vehicle family is a U.S. Army family of eight-wheeled armored vehicles?
questions.explanation_correct: Stryker is the name of the U.S. Army's family of eight-wheeled armored fighting vehicles. It is commonly associated with infantry transport and support roles.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Bradley and M113 are tracked vehicles; LAV-25 is an eight-wheeled vehicle used by the U.S. Marine Corps.

questions.question: Which name is given to the first commercially successful self-propelled torpedo, perfected in Fiume in the 1860s?
questions.explanation_correct: Robert Whitehead refined Giovanni Lupis's ideas into a reliable naval weapon used globally for decades.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Lupis gave the initial concept; Brennan and Simms developed alternative guided or motorized weapons.

questions.question: Which British main battle tank family includes the Challenger 1 and Challenger 2?
questions.explanation_correct: Challenger 1 and Challenger 2 are distinct British main battle tanks within the Challenger family.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Chieftain, Centurion and Cromwell are other British tank designs.

questions.question: Which Belgian rifle family became one of the most widely used battle rifle designs of the 20th century?
questions.explanation_correct: FAL refers to the Fabrique Nationale Fusil Automatique Léger, a Belgian rifle family adopted by many militaries worldwide. It is one of the best-known rifle designs of its era.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are rifle designs, but they are not the Belgian family asked for here. Each is a plausible firearms distractor, yet only FAL is correct.

questions.question: Which German submachine gun introduced in 1940 followed the MP38?
questions.explanation_correct: The MP40 was a German submachine gun widely used in World War II and developed from the earlier MP38.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The MP38 was an earlier German design; Thompson and Sten are American and British designs.

questions.question: What is the official nickname of the F/A-18A–D multirole fighter?
questions.explanation_correct: The F/A-18A–D is named Hornet and was used by the U.S. Navy and Marine Corps.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Falcon and Viper are associated with the F-16, while Raptor names the F-22.

questions.question: The OH-58 is a highly mobile US reconnaissance and light attack helicopter better known by which name?
questions.explanation_correct: The Bell OH-58 Kiowa was primarily used by the US Army for observation and light fire support.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Cayuse is the OH-6; Apache is the AH-64 attack heli; Black Hawk is the UH-60 transport.

questions.question: What is the official name of the U.S. B-1B variable-sweep bomber?
questions.explanation_correct: The B-1B is officially named Lancer; it is also informally known as the Bone.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Stratofortress is the B-52, Superfortress the B-29, and Valkyrie the XB-70.

questions.question: Which Royal Navy aircraft carrier class included HMS Invincible, HMS Illustrious and HMS Ark Royal (R07)?
questions.explanation_correct: The three ships formed the Invincible class.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Queen Elizabeth, Colossus and Majestic are other Royal Navy carrier classes.

questions.question: Which German battleship was sunk in May 1941 after the sinking of HMS Hood?
questions.explanation_correct: Bismarck sank in May 1941 after a pursuit by the Royal Navy.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Tirpitz, Scharnhorst and Gneisenau were different German capital ships.

questions.question: Which Confederate submersible is referred to by the name listed below?
questions.explanation_correct: The Hunley was a Confederate submarine during the American Civil War. It is often cited as an early combat submersible.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are other submarine or submersible names, but they do not fit this Confederate craft.

questions.question: What is the name of the U.S. AIM-9 short-range air-to-air missile?
questions.explanation_correct: The AIM-9 Sidewinder is a short-range air-to-air missile.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Sparrow is another air-to-air missile; Patriot and Nike are surface-to-air systems.

questions.question: What Allied nickname was given to Japan’s Type 93 oxygen-propelled torpedo?
questions.explanation_correct: Long Lance was the Allied nickname for the Japanese Type 93 torpedo.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Kaiten was a Japanese manned torpedo; the other choices are not the Type 93 nickname.

questions.question: What is FN Herstal’s light machine gun also designated M249 in U.S. service?
questions.explanation_correct: The FN Minimi is a light machine gun; the M249 is the U.S. designation for a related version.
questions.explanation_incorrect: MAG, M2 and Bren are different machine guns.

questions.question: Which French 155 mm self-propelled howitzer is mounted on a truck chassis?
questions.explanation_correct: CAESAR is a truck-mounted French self-propelled howitzer.
questions.explanation_incorrect: AUF1 uses a tracked chassis, TRF1 is towed, and Bishop was a British tracked vehicle.

questions.question: What is the name of the Swedish reusable recoilless rifle family designated M3 and M4?
questions.explanation_correct: Carl Gustaf is a Swedish recoilless rifle family that includes the M3 and M4.
questions.explanation_incorrect: AT4, Panzerfaust and Bazooka are different anti-armor weapons; AT4 is also Swedish.

questions.question: Which company name became a common informal name for the German Sd.Kfz. 251 half-track?
questions.explanation_correct: Hanomag was one of the manufacturers associated with the Sd.Kfz. 251 and became an informal name for it.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Krupp, Boeing and Vickers are other companies; the Sd.Kfz. 251 is the vehicle designation.

questions.question: Which British tank was named after a Roman army officer commanding a century?
questions.explanation_correct: Centurion is the name of a British tank that saw extensive postwar service.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Chieftain was also a postwar British main battle tank; Comet and Cromwell were other British tanks.

questions.question: Which FN Herstal rifle family’s name abbreviates “Special Operations Forces Combat Assault Rifle”?
questions.explanation_correct: FN SCAR is a modular rifle family developed by FN Herstal.
questions.explanation_incorrect: FAL and FNC are other FN rifle families; BAR refers to other weapon designs.

questions.question: What is the official nickname of the U.S. F-22 stealth fighter?
questions.explanation_correct: The F-22 is officially named Raptor.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Viper and Falcon are associated with the F-16, while Hornet is the F/A-18.

questions.question: What is the common Russian name for the Kamov Ka-52 coaxial-rotor attack helicopter?
questions.explanation_correct: The Ka-52 is commonly named Alligator; its NATO reporting name is Hokum B.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are helicopter names, but they refer to different models. They do not match the Russian coaxial gunship in the clue.

questions.question: Which U.S. aircraft carrier class included USS Essex (CV-9) and USS Intrepid (CV-11)?
questions.explanation_correct: Essex and Intrepid belonged to the Essex class of U.S. fleet carriers.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Yorktown and Lexington are other classes; Enterprise is a ship name used by several carriers.

questions.question: Which U.S. battleship class included USS Missouri (BB-63) and USS Wisconsin (BB-64)?
questions.explanation_correct: Missouri and Wisconsin were Iowa-class battleships.
questions.explanation_incorrect: North Carolina, South Dakota and Colorado were other U.S. battleship classes named after states.

questions.question: What was the surname of the Israeli designer associated with the Uzi submachine gun?
questions.explanation_correct: Uziel Gal designed the Uzi; the weapon name derives from his given name.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Browning, Kalashnikov and Garand are different firearms designers.

questions.question: Which Swedish company manufactured the barrels for the early Carl Gustaf m/48 recoilless rifle, according to Saab’s company history?
questions.explanation_correct: Saab’s history describes development at FFV in Eskilstuna and barrel manufacturing by Bofors.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Boeing, Lockheed and Beretta are other companies.

questions.question: What British shipborne air-defense missile system carried the designation GWS.30?
questions.explanation_correct: Sea Dart was a British shipborne surface-to-air missile system designated GWS.30.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Sea Wolf was also a naval air-defense system; Sea Skua and Sea Eagle were anti-ship missiles.

questions.question: What is the NATO reporting name of the Tupolev Tu-160 variable-sweep bomber?
questions.explanation_correct: Blackjack is the NATO reporting name for the Tu-160.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Bear is Tu-95, Backfire is Tu-22M and Badger is Tu-16; Backfire is also supersonic.

questions.question: What three-letter abbreviation identifies the Soviet BMP-1 and BMP-2 infantry fighting vehicle family?
questions.explanation_correct: BMP denotes a family of Soviet infantry fighting vehicles including the BMP-1 and BMP-2.
questions.explanation_incorrect: BTR, MT-LB and BRDM designate other Soviet armored vehicle families.

questions.question: Which German machine gun introduced in 1942 became known for a high cyclic rate of fire?
questions.explanation_correct: The MG42 was introduced during World War II and became known for its high rate of fire.
questions.explanation_incorrect: MG34 and MG3 are also German general-purpose machine guns; FG42 was a different weapon.

questions.question: Which U.S. destroyer class includes USS Arleigh Burke (DDG-51)?
questions.explanation_correct: USS Arleigh Burke is the lead ship of the Arleigh Burke class of guided-missile destroyers.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Zumwalt and Spruance are also destroyer classes; Ticonderoga is a cruiser class.

questions.question: Which French self-propelled howitzer is also known as the GCT 155?
questions.explanation_correct: The AuF1, also called GCT 155, is based on the AMX-30 chassis.
questions.explanation_incorrect: CAESAR is truck-mounted, TRF1 is towed, and Bishop was a British self-propelled gun.

questions.question: Which Dassault fighter has single-seat C, carrier-based M and two-seat B variants?
questions.explanation_correct: Dassault Rafale variants include the C, M and B.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Mirage 2000, Mirage F1 and Alpha Jet are different French aircraft designs.

questions.question: Which Soviet medium tank family included the T-34-76 and T-34-85?
questions.explanation_correct: T-34-76 and T-34-85 refer to variants of the Soviet T-34 tank.
questions.explanation_incorrect: T-54, KV-1 and T-80 are different Soviet tank designs.

questions.question: Which Belgian bullpup rifle is developed by FN Herstal?
questions.explanation_correct: The FN F2000 is a bullpup rifle manufactured by the Belgian company FN Herstal.
questions.explanation_incorrect: FAMAS is French, SA80 is British, and Steyr AUG is Austrian.

questions.question: Which world-famous submachine gun was developed by the German manufacturer Heckler & Koch post-World War II?
questions.explanation_correct: The MP5 is a H&K submachine gun introduced in the 1960s, long after WWII.
questions.explanation_incorrect: MP40 and StG 44 are WWII-era German weapons, and PPSh-41 is Soviet-era.

questions.question: Which U.S. general-purpose machine gun used in Vietnam was nicknamed “the Pig”?
questions.explanation_correct: The M60 machine gun was nicknamed “the Pig” during the Vietnam War.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The M240, M1919 and BAR are different American military weapon designations.

questions.question: What is the official name of the McDonnell Douglas F-4 fighter?
questions.explanation_correct: The F-4 is named Phantom II.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Mustang, Thunderbolt and Tomcat are names associated with other aircraft.

questions.question: What official name does the U.S. A-10 close-support jet share with the earlier P-47 fighter?
questions.explanation_correct: The A-10 is officially Thunderbolt II; the earlier P-47 was named Thunderbolt.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Corsair, Skyhawk and Valkyrie are names of other aircraft.

questions.question: Which Soviet design bureau created the Tu-160 variable-sweep strategic bomber?
questions.explanation_correct: Tupolev designed the Tu-160 strategic bomber.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Mikoyan, Ilyushin and Sukhoi are other Soviet aerospace design bureaus.

questions.question: Which Royal Navy battlecruiser was sunk by Bismarck in May 1941?
questions.explanation_correct: HMS Hood was sunk in the Battle of the Denmark Strait in 1941. She was launched in 1918.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Renown, Repulse and Invincible were different British battlecruisers.

questions.question: Which famous Royal Navy name was carried by the 1930s carrier that served in WWII and its post-war modern namesake?
questions.explanation_correct: The HMS Ark Royal was a legendary carrier known for its role in hunting the Bismarck.
questions.explanation_incorrect: While these are all British carrier names, Ark Royal is the most iconic series of ships in this lineage.

questions.question: Which German U-boat type was produced in the largest numbers during World War II?
questions.explanation_correct: Type VII was the most numerous German U-boat type of World War II.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Types IX, XXI and II were other German submarine types.

questions.question: Which Soviet surface-to-air missile family includes the S-300P?
questions.explanation_correct: S-300P belongs to the S-300 family of surface-to-air missile systems.
questions.explanation_incorrect: S-75, S-125 and S-400 are other Soviet or Russian systems.

questions.question: What French nickname means “seventy-five” and refers to the 1897 75 mm field gun?
questions.explanation_correct: Soixante-Quinze means seventy-five and is associated with the French 75 mm field gun.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Grosse Bertha was a German artillery nickname; Schneider and de Bange are artillery-related names.

questions.question: What U.S. World War II half-track designation was shared by an armored personnel carrier and its variants, such as the M3A1?
questions.explanation_correct: The M3 Half-track family included the M3A1 armored personnel carrier.
questions.explanation_incorrect: M2, M5 and M9 were related but distinct half-track designations.

questions.question: What was the name of Japan’s manned suicide torpedo used during the Pacific War?
questions.explanation_correct: Kaiten was a Japanese manned suicide torpedo used in World War II.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Shinyo was an explosive boat, Ohka a piloted rocket aircraft, and Kikka a jet aircraft.

questions.question: What is the official name of the Lockheed C-130 transport aircraft?
questions.explanation_correct: The Lockheed C-130 is named Hercules.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Dakota, Cargomaster and Globemaster are names associated with other transport aircraft.

questions.question: Which German main battle tank family includes the Leopard 1 and Leopard 2?
questions.explanation_correct: Leopard is the family name of the Leopard 1 and Leopard 2 main battle tanks.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Panther and Tiger were World War II tanks; Marder is an infantry fighting vehicle.

questions.question: Which of these is a rifle model designation associated with Belgian firearms manufacturer FN Herstal?
questions.explanation_correct: The FN FAL is a famous battle rifle designed and manufactured by the Belgian company Fabrique Nationale (FN).
questions.explanation_incorrect: The G3 is German, the AKM is Soviet, and the M16 is American.

questions.question: What informal nickname is used for the F-16 Fighting Falcon?
questions.explanation_correct: Viper is a common informal nickname for the F-16, whose official name is Fighting Falcon.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Hornet, Tomcat and Eagle are associated with other fighter aircraft.

questions.question: What is the NATO reporting name for the Mil Mi-28 attack helicopter?
questions.explanation_correct: Havoc is the NATO reporting name for the Mi-28.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Hind is Mi-24, Hip is Mi-8, and Hook is Mi-6.

questions.question: Which Japanese battleship class included Yamato and Musashi?
questions.explanation_correct: Yamato and Musashi were Yamato-class battleships.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Nagato, Kongō and Fusō were different Japanese battleship classes.

questions.question: Which of these is an iconic Israeli-designed submachine gun?
questions.explanation_correct: The Uzi is a world-famous Israeli submachine gun designed by Uziel Gal in the late 1940s.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Jericho is a pistol, while Galil and Tavor are assault rifles.

questions.question: Which French aircraft carrier is named after the leader of Free France during World War II?
questions.explanation_correct: Charles de Gaulle is a French aircraft carrier named after the French leader.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Clemenceau and Foch were also French aircraft carriers; Richelieu was a battleship.

questions.question: What onomatopoeic nickname was used for the British QF 2-pounder automatic naval gun?
questions.explanation_correct: The British QF 2-pounder automatic gun was nicknamed the pom-pom.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Bofors, Oerlikon and Vickers are manufacturers or gun-associated names.

questions.question: What Russian name is associated with the S-400 air-defense system?
questions.explanation_correct: Triumf is the Russian name associated with the S-400 system.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Buk, S-300 and Tor are also surface-to-air missile system names, but are different systems.

questions.question: Which American armored vehicle family includes the M2 infantry fighting vehicle and M3 cavalry fighting vehicle?
questions.explanation_correct: The Bradley family includes the M2 and M3 fighting vehicles.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Stryker is a wheeled vehicle family, M113 is an armored personnel carrier, and Abrams is a tank.

questions.question: Which Soviet strategic bomber is commonly known by the nickname that refers to a large ursine animal?
questions.explanation_correct: Bear is the NATO reporting name for the Tupolev Tu-95, a Soviet strategic bomber. It is widely associated with that nickname.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are also military codenames or aircraft-related names, but they do not identify the Tu-95. They belong to different aircraft or weapon systems.

questions.question: What was the German nickname for the World War II G7es T5 acoustic-homing torpedo?
questions.explanation_correct: Zaunkönig was the German nickname for the G7es T5 acoustic-homing torpedo.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Kaiten was a Japanese manned torpedo; the other choices are not the requested nickname.

questions.question: What nickname was given to the U.S. M7 self-propelled howitzer?
questions.explanation_correct: Priest was the nickname of the M7 105 mm self-propelled howitzer.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Sexton, Bishop and Wespe were different self-propelled guns.

questions.question: Which British destroyer class name is also a common English adjective meaning bold or forceful?
questions.explanation_correct: Daring was a British destroyer class used by the Royal Navy. It is the class name requested by the question.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices are also Royal Navy class names, but they are not the specific class asked for. They identify different destroyer or cruiser classes.

questions.question: What is the common name of the U.S. Mk 153 83 mm Shoulder-Launched Multipurpose Assault Weapon?
questions.explanation_correct: The Mk 153 SMAW is the Shoulder-Launched Multipurpose Assault Weapon.
questions.explanation_incorrect: M72 LAW, Carl Gustaf and AT4 are different systems.

questions.question: Which Soviet tank family includes the T-72A and T-72B?
questions.explanation_correct: The T-72A and T-72B are variants of the T-72 main battle tank.
questions.explanation_incorrect: T-64 and T-80 variants also use autoloaders and 125 mm guns; T-55 is an earlier design.

questions.question: Which bullpup rifle was developed by the Austrian company Steyr?
questions.explanation_correct: The Steyr AUG is an Austrian bullpup rifle.
questions.explanation_incorrect: FN FAL is Belgian, HK G36 German, and AR-18 American in origin.

questions.question: Which compact firearm is a small version of the Israeli Uzi submachine-gun family?
questions.explanation_correct: The Micro Uzi is a compact variant of the Uzi family.
questions.explanation_incorrect: MAC-10, MP5K and Skorpion are other compact firearms.

questions.question: What is a common informal nickname of the F-16 Fighting Falcon?
questions.explanation_correct: Viper is a common informal F-16 nickname; Fighting Falcon is the aircraft’s official name.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Hornet refers to the F/A-18; Eagle refers to the F-15; Falcon is the official but less used name.

questions.question: What is the common Russian name for the Kamov Ka-52 attack helicopter?
questions.explanation_correct: The Ka-52 is commonly called Alligator; its NATO reporting name is Hokum B.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Hind, Havoc and Hip are NATO reporting names for other helicopters.

questions.question: What is the name of the modern class of 65,000-tonne supercarriers currently in service with the Royal Navy?
questions.explanation_correct: The Queen Elizabeth-class includes the HMS Queen Elizabeth and HMS Prince of Wales.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Invincible was a carrier class; Ark Royal and Illustrious are names used for several Royal Navy ships.

questions.question: Which German Deutschland-class ship was renamed Lützow in 1940?
questions.explanation_correct: The Deutschland-class armored ship Deutschland was renamed Lützow in 1940.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Admiral Graf Spee was another Deutschland-class ship; Scharnhorst and Bismarck belonged to other classes.

questions.question: What alternative name is used for the French AuF1 155 mm self-propelled howitzer?
questions.explanation_correct: The AuF1 is also known as GCT 155 and uses an AMX-30-derived chassis.
questions.explanation_incorrect: CAESAR, TRF1 and Bishop are different artillery systems.

questions.question: Which 84mm unguided, man-portable, single-shot Swedish weapon is used by the US military as the M136?
questions.explanation_correct: The AT4 is a disposable anti-armor weapon designed by Saab Bofors Dynamics.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Carl Gustaf is reusable, NLAW is a guided system, and M72 LAW is a different disposable launcher.

questions.question: The RIM-66 and RIM-156 belong to which primary family of shipborne surface-to-air missiles?
questions.explanation_correct: The RIM-66 and RIM-156 are variants within the Standard Missile family used for naval air defense.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Sea Sparrow is a separate air-defense system; Tomahawk and Harpoon serve other roles.

questions.question: Which U.S. Navy heavyweight torpedo was designed for launch from submarines?
questions.explanation_correct: The Mk 48 is a U.S. heavyweight torpedo used by submarines.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Mk 46, Mk 50 and Mk 54 are different lightweight torpedo designs.

questions.question: The M998 HMMWV, developed by AM General for the US military, is universally known by which name?
questions.explanation_correct: Humvee is a phonetic derivation of the HMMWV (High Mobility Multipurpose Wheeled Vehicle) acronym.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Jeep was its predecessor; JLTV is its modern replacement; M998 is a specific model number.

questions.question: Which NATO reporting name was assigned to the Tupolev Tu-22M swing-wing long-range bomber?
questions.explanation_correct: The Tu-22M Backfire was designed for maritime strike and strategic bombing during the Cold War.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Bear is the Tu-95, Blackjack is the Tu-160, and Badger is the Tu-16.

questions.question: Which Soviet-designed rocket launcher entered service in the early 1960s as a successor to the RPG-2?
questions.explanation_correct: The RPG-7 is a Soviet-designed launcher that followed the RPG-2.
questions.explanation_incorrect: RPG-2 was an earlier Soviet launcher; M72 LAW and Carl Gustaf are different weapons.

questions.question: What is the name of the US Navy's radar-guided 20mm Gatling gun system used to destroy incoming missiles?
questions.explanation_correct: The Phalanx CIWS is colloquially known as 'R2-D2' due to its distinct white dome.
questions.explanation_incorrect: SeaRAM uses missiles; Goalkeeper is Dutch-made; Crotale is a French missile system.

questions.question: Which British tank name is associated with a World War II heavy tank?
questions.explanation_correct: Churchill was the name of a British heavy tank used during World War II. It is one of the best-known British tank names from that era.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Cromwell and Comet were British cruiser tanks; Centurion was a later British tank.

questions.question: Which designer surname is associated with the AR-15 family of rifles?
questions.explanation_correct: Eugene Stoner designed the AR-10 and AR-15 platforms. His surname is strongly associated with these rifles.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names are famous firearms designers, but they are not tied to the AR-15 family. They represent different weapons and design lineages.

questions.question: Which nickname is commonly linked to the F-104 interceptor?
questions.explanation_correct: The Lockheed F-104 is commonly known as the Starfighter. That nickname is widely used in aviation history.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are nicknames for different fighter aircraft. They do not identify the F-104.

questions.question: Which weapon name refers to a well-known American submachine gun from the 1920s?
questions.explanation_correct: The Thompson submachine gun is a classic American firearm introduced in the early 20th century. It is one of the most recognizable SMGs in history.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are submachine guns too, but they are different models from other countries or periods. They are not the Thompson.

questions.question: Which European attack helicopter model name was developed jointly by France and Germany?
questions.explanation_correct: The Eurocopter Tiger is a European attack helicopter developed by France and Germany. Its model name is Tiger.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are attack helicopter models as well, but they are not the French-German design. They belong to different programs and countries.

questions.question: Which German battleship class included Scharnhorst and Gneisenau?
questions.explanation_correct: Scharnhorst and Gneisenau formed the Scharnhorst class.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Bismarck was also a two-ship battleship class, consisting of Bismarck and Tirpitz; Deutschland was another class.

questions.question: What does the acronym LAW stand for in the M72 LAW designation?
questions.explanation_correct: LAW stands for Light Anti-tank Weapon; the M72 is a disposable system.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other expansions are not the meaning of LAW in the M72 designation.

questions.question: Which U.S. carrier class included USS Midway (CV-41), commissioned in 1945?
questions.explanation_correct: USS Midway was the lead ship of the Midway class and was commissioned in 1945.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Nimitz, Essex and Yorktown were different U.S. carrier classes.

questions.question: What nickname was applied to Soviet multiple rocket launchers such as the BM-13 in World War II?
questions.explanation_correct: Katyusha was a common nickname for Soviet wartime rocket launchers such as the BM-13.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Grad is a later Soviet rocket system; HIMARS and M270 are American systems.

questions.question: The RIM-7 Sea Sparrow shipborne missile was developed from which air-to-air missile?
questions.explanation_correct: The RIM-7 Sea Sparrow was developed from the AIM-7 Sparrow air-to-air missile.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Sidewinder is a different air-to-air missile; Harpoon and Tomahawk are missiles with different roles.
